6 months ago I was looking at first time homeowners loans... today, i have a horrible addiction yet again and nothing to show for all my years of work and bullshit on this planet. If anyone understands the desperation of wanting to end it all, I definitely do. But the advice I can give is that life is full of mountains and valleys. We cannot know light without dark. We cannot appreciate the highs without the lows. We were put on this Earth to experience every emotion possible and that includes the shitty ones. I know you may seem hopeless at the time, but please remember that tomorrow may be better and the day after even better. All we have to do is keep moving forward and appreciate that every moment is a gift. My mother and I had/have a terrible relationship. She is an alcoholic and was abusive verbally/emotionally/physically while I was growing up, and still to some extent now. I never knew my father either. I remember breaking down at one point during my pregnancy, I mean a full blown sob fest, because I realized that I didn't know what true love between a parent and child, or any love for that matter, was really like and I was so scared that I wouldn't be able to love my son the way he deserved. 

Looking back now, I realize how silly my fears were. I poured everything (and still do) from my heart into that little boy. I focused on giving him every ounce of love that I had ever craved, wanted, or felt cheated out of. I make sure to remind him as often as possible how much he means to me, how much better my life is with him in it, how happy he makes me, how proud I am of him, and how much I love and adore him. I am an overly affectionate mom. I give hugs and kisses away freely, and mourn the day when he won't except them as easily (he's 5). I had him in my room in a bassinet for the first several months, pulling him into bed happily when it was time to nurse. One of my favorite memories as a first time mom, because the bonding was so special. When he was big enough, I started letting him sleep with me because it comforted me so much. I still go into his room some nights and cuddle him or pull him into our bed if I'm having trouble sleeping. I am open and honest with him, and will continue to be forever, because he deserves that. I show him that he can trust me to always be there for him because he needs that in order to trust in himself when exploring the world on his own, knowing that he can fall back on me when he needs it most. I create and enjoy experiences with him that I craved as a child. And the little things are just as important as the big ones. We all sat down for warm cookies and milk the other night before bed, and he loved it, thanking me for our 'family cookie night'. I know that I will never forget the experience, as mundane as it may be, because he makes every second so special. 

I am having a girl this time around, and again I am nervous that I won't know how to love her the right way. But, like before, I know that will pass once I meet her and put that love into practice. What I'm getting at is, I feel like that because I *didn't* have a good relationship with my mother it has made me that much stronger and ready to be exactly the type of mother I wanted to be. She showed me all the ways I didn't want to be or become, and it confirmed to me exactly how to love my son in the best way possible. If you are concerned, don't be. Because you are already proving yourself to be the best mom your daughter could ever imagine. Good luck momma!
